patches.new_disclaimer: AVAs that span state lines are counted for each state they touch, so totals sum to more than the 279 recognized AVAs. DC not included (source omits it).
Counts each trail once per state it enters. National Scenic Trails (Appalachian Trail, Pacific Crest Trail, etc.) are a separate program and are not included here. Includes Washington DC.
Counts notable annual rodeos listed on Wikipedia; not every county-fair rodeo is included. DC not included (source omits it).
Counts festivals listed by Wikipedia as recurring notable events, past and present. Includes Washington DC.
Counts all convention and civic exhibition venues listed on the Wikipedia page, including smaller regional facilities as well as major convention halls. Includes Washington DC.

Values reflect the single largest state fair in each state as reported on Wikipedia, not the sum of multiple regional fairs. Attendance years vary because state fairs report at different times. DC not included (topic is state-scoped).
National Historic Trails are administered separately and are not counted here. Each trail counts once per state it enters. DC not included (source omits it).

Only units carrying the 'National Park' designation are considered — national monuments, seashores, historic sites, and recreation areas are excluded. Parks spanning two states are credited to each state; the value shown is that state's single busiest park. DC not included (source omits it).
Refuges whose boundaries cross state lines are counted in the state where the main visitor entrance is located, per the source's convention. DC not included (source omits it).

Wikipedia's list uses a broad definition that includes regional parks, kiddie parks, family entertainment centers, and some seasonal parks. Central Florida's parks are counted from a linked sub-list. DC not included (source omits it).
Counts monuments administered by all federal agencies (NPS, BLM, USFS, USFWS, etc.), not just the National Park Service. Monuments that span two states are counted in each. Includes Washington DC.
Counts every state a byway passes through, so byways spanning multiple states are credited to each. Hawaii and Texas have no designated byways. DC not included (source omits it).
Counts all lighthouses identified by the US Coast Guard on each state's Wikipedia list, including active, deactivated, destroyed, and historic structures. DC not included (source omits it).
